$comment: Every entry needs a reason that says why the flaw is not reachable in THIS repo, not merely
that upgrading is inconvenient. Every entry also needs a reviewBy date: the gate fails once it
passes, so an exception cannot quietly become permanent. The gate also fails on entries that no
longer match a finding, so a fixed package cannot leave its exception behind.

accepted.reason: Covers ONLY the zod 3.25.x copy nested under @ag-ui/client and @ag-ui/core in both frontends (#939). The flaw makes an array schema allocate one issue per failing element, so a huge array of malformed elements can exhaust memory. No zod 3.x release has the fix (first patched: 4.6.6), the latest @ag-ui (1.0.3) still requires zod ^3.25.76, and forcing it onto zod 4 with an npm override breaks @ag-ui at runtime (its single-argument z.record(...) throws under zod 4). Reachability: @ag-ui runs only in the browser and validates the event stream from the harness's own AgentHub (/ag-ui/run, same origin, authenticated). AgentHub is .NET and serialises typed events, so the arrays in that stream are well-formed; model and tool output can only fill string fields, which cannot make an element fail. The worst case is the viewer's own tab running out of memory, and nothing server-side runs this code. Each frontend's own top-level zod is patched (^4.6.7 in WebUI's package.json, 4.6.7 locked in both), and that floor is what stops this entry from hiding a regression of it, because the gate matches by package name. Remove when @ag-ui ships on zod >= 4.6.6.
